sources.note: Nothing on stress. Lists 'brk beraku' with sole source 'Caprile 1972'; places beraku among the 'parlers septentrionaux (bulala, beraku, kenga, 'barma) occupant une situation indécise ou ambivalente' (the text layer); the family is described as tonal (2 registers *SBB, a third register innovated in the western languages).

sources.citation: Bouquet, Christian (1976). Aperçu démographique et socio-économique du groupe babalia (Tchad). Cahiers d'études africaines 16(63-64): 615-626.
sources.note: Demographic study; says the language (Brage / Beraku) is being replaced by Chadian Arabic or Kotoko and that in 1974 only 39 elders of 1,699 Babalia still spoke it; no linguistic description, nothing on stress or tone. Persée PDF is behind an altcha challenge; page text read via direct download.
